title: Jean-Jacques F NDE 9998
content:
9998:

FIRST NDE - 7 YEARS OF AGE

This is my first NDE experience which occurred when I was 7 years old. I will experience 2 other NDEs in my lifetime: the second one at 38 years old and the third one two days before my 39th birthday. These experiences are shared separately.

At a very young age, I was diagnosed with acute rheumatic fever following a severe Streptococcus microbial infection. This inflammatory disease mostly affected my cardiovascular system resulting in valve damages and an enlarged heart. Doctors strongly recommended to my parents that I have my tonsils surgically removed as a preventative measure. This was back in 1959, well before the advent of our universal health care system in Canada.

Not having much money, my parents had to shop around to find the lowest price for this surgery. My father never had a car so my parents and I used public transportation to get to the 'clinic' to have my tonsils removed that fateful day.

Upon arrival, I noticed that many children were sitting with their parents in the waiting room. As the awful smell of ether forebode an imminent danger, our mournful cries were our last desperate attempt to convince them to return home and forego such a frightful and insane scheme. Innocently, we thought that we would be subjected to yet another inoculation. But what was to come would be far more traumatic than a mere vaccination.

A nurse entered the room and called a few names. I prayed that mine would never be pronounced, but in vain. I begged my parents to immediately go back home. Instead, they accompanied me (or rather dragged me) to a small room where they took off my clothes, dressed me in a sterile gown and placed me on a stretcher. The nurse came back in and gave me an injection to calm me down.

The smell of ether was getting more and more intense. This was a sure sign that the worst was yet to come. Another nurse entered the room and told my parents to return to the waiting room. The nurse walked over to the head of the stretcher, disengaged the brake and wheeled me to the operating room. I held back my tears because we all know that 'boys don't cry'. I was all alone in the world to face the surgery.

After entering the room, I was immediately transferred onto a hard table. A rubber mask was abruptly placed over my face and I was forced to breathe the suffocating odor of chloroform gas. I tried to struggle but my body was unresponsive. My eyelids became heavier and then nothingness.

Suddenly, I felt myself floating face down over my body and rising up towards the ceiling as an unusual feeling of great peace and well-being overwhelmed me. I noticed three masked individuals in surgical gowns standing below me. They were leaning over a long table and seemed quite upset and agitated. There was a sort of humming sound in my ears so I couldn’t hear their conversation.

The door flew open and a fourth individual in garbs came running in. He appeared quite irritated and was yelling at the others. I still couldn't hear a thing as the humming noise was getting even louder. Was I dreaming? If so, never had I experienced such a marvelous dream filled with serenity, joy and love so intense that mere words cannot describe. These powerful emotions were new to me and yet, they felt so very familiar.

Without any fear or concern, I floated to the other side of the room. I noticed a child lying on the table. As I took a closer look, I realized that it was me! I was in no way shocked or terrified by this awareness, quite the contrary. I felt very euphoric as it seemed to be a normal phenomenon and even a joyous and sublime omen.

The humming in my ears intensified. It suddenly stopped when a long and upward dark tunnel appeared behind me at about a 45-degree angle. I saw a bright white light glowing at its furthest point. It was like standing at one end of a long train tunnel and staring at the beam of light from the locomotive entering at the other end.

I felt a pulling force as an energy was beckoning me to enter the vortex. Without any fear or hesitation, I slowly floated towards its entrance. I was overwhelmed with feelings of Happiness, peace, unconditional love and excitement. It was as though I was returning home after a long trip abroad, eagerly looking forward to reuniting again with family and dear friends. I made my way through the tunnel with increasing speed in a clockwise spiral motion. I heard sublime music which no words can describe. It could be compared with the most beautiful classical music ever composed. My eyes easily fill with tears when I relive that mystic experience listening to specific musical pieces composed by classical masters.

As I got closer to the light, I felt intense feelings of unconditional love and exceptional peace. I could stare directly at its brilliance even though it seemed far brighter than when looking directly at the sun. I had no sorrow nor regret for having been 'taken away' from my parents, my brother and others whom I love as I knew for sure that I was still constantly with them. Suddenly, I came to a standstill and was promptly pushed away in the opposite direction at a dizzying speed. I excruciatingly reintegrating the little boy’s body on the operation table.

As I opened my eyes in the recovery room, a terrible torment invaded my whole body and my throat seemed to be on fire. My mother was at my bedside with tears in her eyes. The white sheets were covered with blood. With unbearable pain, I repeatedly vomited blood.

How I wished I could instantly return to my marvelous 'dream' where I was completely freed of my sorrow and pain. I implored my mother that we return home. She answered that the doctor wanted to keep me under observation for a while longer. Later that evening, the doctor finally told my parents that we could go home although I was still quite feverish and still vomiting blood. My father called for a taxi. Noticing my condition, the taxi driver placed some newspapers on the car’s floor to protect it.

Up until my teenage years, I thought that my out-of-body experience had only been a dream or an hallucination although it still remained quite fresh in my mind throughout all those years. Even now writing these lines, my eyes fill with tears as these memories still have a powerful effect on me. It was only when I read Doctor Raymond Moody's book titled Life After Life that I discovered that millions of people throughout the world have had similar experiences regardless of their age, nationality, race, culture or faith.

The dangers of using chloroform (ether) for anesthesia had been well known to the medical community ever since its discovery. These risks were greater still in regards to children as was clearly indicated in the medical work titled Chloroform in the Surgery of Children published in 1875 (Adrien Delahaye, publisher). Obviously, the use of this anesthetic chemical by competent individuals in a reputable hospital environment greatly reduced the incidence of tragic results. Such was not the case back in 1959 when I had my tonsils removed in a makeshift clinic at the lowest price available.

tunnel.movement_other_detail: Moved through the tunnel "with increasing speed in a clockwise spiral motion" and heard "sublime music."

context.nde_cause_other_detail: Tonsil removal surgery under chloroform/ether anesthesia; child had acute rheumatic fever and heart enlargement/valve damage.

stage_sequence.sequence_variation_description: OBE in operating room followed by appearance of a dark upward tunnel with bright white light; then abrupt push back and rapid return to body.

unique_elements.nonstandard_elements: He reported a loud "humming" that intensified then stopped when the tunnel appeared; tunnel was "upward" at about a 45-degree angle and travel was in a "clockwise spiral" with "sublime music."
unique_elements.notable_quotes: "I felt myself floating face down over my body and rising up towards the ceiling"; "a long and upward dark tunnel appeared behind me at about a 45-degree angle"; "I was overwhelmed with feelings of Happiness, peace, unconditional love"; "It was as though I was returning home after a long trip abroad"; "mere words cannot describe."
